historical_record.description: Built in 1932 for the Japanese YWCA to a design by Julia Morgan, paid for from within the Japantown community and by the national and San Francisco YWCAs. It held a dormitory for ten, classrooms and meeting rooms, a library and an office, and appears to be the only building in the United States purpose-built by and for Issei women. Because the Alien Land Law barred Issei from owning property, the San Francisco YWCA held the title in trust for the community.

After the war the American Friends Service Committee used the building and let returning Japanese American women organise activities and take shelter there. The Japanese YWCA was not re-formed; it joined the Buchanan YMCA instead, making the first combined YWCA/YMCA in the country.

When the San Francisco YWCA announced plans to sell the building, which then housed a bilingual pre-school, community members went to law to establish the Japanese American community's claim to it, and succeeded.
Recorded in the city's 2009 survey of Japantown as the Japantown YWCA, taken as representative of the neighborhood's community centres and social halls.
